subject: Religious and Moral Education
name: JHS 2 Religious and Moral Education
description: The JHS 2 Religious and Moral Education curriculum deepens learners' understanding of creation stories, religious practices such as rites of passage, the role of authority and obedience in the family and community, the exemplary lives of religious leaders, moral teachings, and economic life including the wise use of money and avoiding bribery and corruption.

strands.title: GOD, HIS CREATION AND ATTRIBUTES
strands.description: Understanding creation stories and their moral lessons.

subStrands.title: THE CREATION STORIES OF THE THREE MAJOR RELIGIONS IN GHANA
subStrands.description: Creation stories and their moral values.

contentStandards.description: Outline and explain the moral lessons in the creation stories of the three main religions in Ghana

indicators.description: Discuss the creation stories of the three main religions in Ghana

exemplars.description: Give account of the creation stories in the various religions: Christianity (Genesis chapter 1), Islam (Qur'an 2:164, 3:190-191, 10:3-4) and Indigenous African Religion (Narrate oral traditions of learners' indigenous society).
In three groups, learners dramatise their own interpretation of the creation stories.

indicators.description: Identify and explain the moral values in each of the creation stories

exemplars.description: Brainstorm to identify the moral values in each of the creation stories. E.g. hard work, orderliness, creativity, responsibility, caring and giving.
In groups, learners dramatise how they apply the moral values in their daily life.

strands.title: RELIGIOUS PRACTICES
strands.description: Rites of passage and their significance.

subStrands.title: RITES OF PASSAGE
subStrands.description: Naming ceremonies, puberty rites, marriage, and death rites.

contentStandards.description: Explain rites of passage and identify the moral lessons in them

indicators.description: Describe the naming ceremonies/outdooring in the three major religions

exemplars.description: Explain the meaning of rites of passage.
Identify the various stages in human life: Birth, Puberty, Marriage, Death.
Identify factors to be considered in choosing a name for a child.
Describe how the naming ceremony is performed in the three major religions (Christianity, Islam, Indigenous).
Discuss importance of naming ceremonies.
Learners to role play a naming ceremony in their community.

indicators.description: Explain physical and emotional changes that characterise puberty

exemplars.description: Explain the meaning of puberty.
Discuss physical and emotional changes that occur at puberty for boys and girls.

indicators.description: Describe how puberty rites are performed in traditional Ghanaian societies

exemplars.description: Describe activities performed during puberty in some Traditional Societies (e.g. Bragro, Dipo, Baala, Sodji-wi).
Learners to role play how puberty rites are performed in their community.
Identify the significance of puberty rites.
In two groups, learners debate the motion 'Puberty rites are outmoded'.

indicators.description: Describe how a marriage is contracted in the three main religions in Ghana

exemplars.description: Explain the term marriage.
Describe how marriage is performed in the three major religions (Indigenous African Religion, Christianity, Islam).
In three groups, learners use a short sketch to demonstrate how marriage rites are performed in each of the three religions.
Identify and explain the importance of marriage rites.

indicators.description: Describe how death rites are performed in the three major religions in Ghana

exemplars.description: Explain the concept of death in the three major religions.
In three groups, learner's role play how death rites are performed in the three religions.
Identify and explain the importance of death rites.

indicators.description: Identify and explain the moral lessons in the rites of passage

exemplars.description: Discuss the moral lessons in the rites of passage (e.g. Truthfulness, Honesty, Hard work).
Dramatise how to apply the moral lessons from rites of passage in their everyday life activities.

contentStandards.description: Identify and explain the importance of obeying authority

indicators.description: Identify and explain the various sources of authority

exemplars.description: Identify the sources of authority at home, school and community.
Using a video clip or pictures, identify how people come to have authority.
In groups learners dramatise the right and wrong use of authority.

indicators.description: Explain the need to obey God, parents and those in authority

exemplars.description: Learners to identify and discuss different reasons for obeying authority.

indicators.description: Demonstrate how to apply the rules and regulations from authority in daily life

exemplars.description: Dramatise how to apply rules and regulations from authority (Home/family, School, Communal, Religious, National).

strands.title: RELIGIOUS LEADERS AND PERSONALITIES
strands.description: Lives and missions of prophets and caliphs.

subStrands.title: PROPHETS AND CALIPHS
subStrands.description: Mission and moral lessons from prophets and caliphs.

contentStandards.description: Identify and explain the moral lessons that can be learned from the exemplary lives of the prophets and caliphs

indicators.description: Describe the mission of the prophets

exemplars.description: Explain the meaning of a prophet.
Watch video clips and/or pictures of prophets in both Christianity and Islam.
Identify some prophets in the video or the pictures.
Read part of the Qur'an and the Bible on the selected prophets (Noah/Nuh, Abraham/Ibrahim, Moses/Musah) and discuss their background, call and mission.

indicators.description: Outline the mission and exemplary lives of the Caliphs

exemplars.description: Explain the meaning of Caliph in Islam.
Identify the Caliphs (Abu Bakr, Umar, Usman, Ali).
State the contributions of the Caliphs.

indicators.description: Examine lessons from the exemplary lives of the Prophets and Caliphs

exemplars.description: Identify and explain the moral lessons in the lives of the prophets and the Caliphs (e.g. Patriotism, Perseverance, Courage).
Dramatise aspects of the lives of the prophet and the Caliphs.
Project Work: Write an essay on the mission of each of the three named prophets and the Caliphs.

subStrands.title: MORAL TEACHINGS IN THE THREE MAJOR RELIGIONS IN GHANA
subStrands.description: Teachings from scriptures and oral traditions.

contentStandards.description: Exemplify the moral teachings from the Bible, Qur'an and Oral Traditions

indicators.description: Identify and explain the moral teachings from the Bible, Qur'an and Oral Traditions

exemplars.description: Learners discuss examples to identify key moral teachings of the three major religions (Christian, Islam, Indigenous African Religion, Proverbs, Taboos).

indicators.description: Demonstrate how to apply the moral teachings from the three main religions in their daily life

exemplars.description: Discuss the application of the moral teachings in their daily life.
Dramatise the moral teachings of the three major religions.

subStrands.title: MONEY
subStrands.description: Wise use and honest acquisition of money.

contentStandards.description: Plan the wise use of money

indicators.description: Explain the term "money" and indicate its usefulness

exemplars.description: Look at pictures of money or real Ghanaian currency notes and coins, and explain the meaning of money and its usefulness.

indicators.description: Identify and explain honest ways of acquiring money

exemplars.description: In groups, learners explain the honest ways of acquiring money as taught by the three major religions.
Give reasons for acquiring money honestly.
Develop habit of saving money for future use.

indicators.description: Discuss the appropriate ways of using money

exemplars.description: Learners brainstorm to identify good ways of using money from the perspective of the three major religions.
Discuss bad ways of using money from the perspective of the three religions.
Put learners into two groups to come out with a sketch to demonstrate a good way and a bad way of using money.

indicators.description: Discuss the benefits of the SSNIT pension scheme and people who are qualified to benefit

exemplars.description: Discuss the SSNIT Pension Scheme, who qualifies, and the roles of employer/employee.

contentStandards.description: Explain the need to avoid bribery and corruption and the ways to do so

indicators.description: Explain the terms "bribery" and "corruption"

exemplars.description: Differentiate between 'bribery' and 'corruption'.

indicators.description: Identify the causes and effects of bribery and corruption

exemplars.description: In groups, learners identify the causes of bribery and corruption.
Using Think-Pair and Share, learners discuss the effects of bribery and corruption on the state.
Explain the need to avoid bribery and corruption.
Examine the moral values that can be used to address bribery and corruption.
